newsitem.title: INDIA: India's exports to improve in 2nd half of 96/97.
newsitem.headline: India's exports to improve in 2nd half of 96/97.

text.p: India's Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah expected export growth to pick up in the second of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March), a government statement said on Wednesday.

The statment quoted Ramaiah as saying at a meeting of parliament deputies on Tuesday that India achieved a export growth rate of 9.9 percent against a target of 18-20 percent in the first six months of the fiscal year ending next March 31.
"India's export rate is expected to improve in second half of the current financial year," the statement quoting Ramaiah said.

He said electronic goods, cotton yarn, raw cotton, wool and manufactures, coffee, agro and allied products such as wheat, spices, seasame seeds, groundnut, oilmeals, molasses and processed foods recorded a high growth rate in the first half of 96/97.
Negative growth rate was registered by gems, jewellery, leather manufactures and iron ore, he said.
"High cost of export finance and infrastructural weaknesses were among the major constrainst impeding exports," Ramaiah said.
He said sluggish export growth trend was recorded by textiles, which accounts for 28 percent of India's total exports.
Similar trends were also witnessed for gems and jewellery, which accounts for 18 percent of India's exports and leather products, which accounts for four percent.
"Thus, the three taken together accounted for 50 percent of the country's exports and this naturally reflected the country's overall export performance," the statement said.
